### Observed differences

- In the earlier window, the elapsed time between the completions of A02 and A08 was typically about 0.9 hours (median 0.88 h, mean 0.87 h over 40 observed consecutive pairs); in the later window it was typically about 1.7 hours (median 1.70 h, mean 1.68 h over 33 pairs) — roughly double, with a wider spread (standard deviation about 0.14 h versus 0.30 h). [TWAIT001]
- In the earlier window, the elapsed time between the completions of A06 and A08 was typically about 0.12 hours (mean 0.13 h over 45 pairs); in the later window it was typically about 0.23 hours (mean 0.33 h over 35 pairs) — the mean rose about two-and-a-half-fold and the spread roughly tripled (standard deviation about 0.09 h versus 0.30 h). [TWAIT002]
- In both pairs the whole distribution shifted upward (all quartiles higher in the later window), while the number of observed consecutive pairs fell modestly (40 to 33, and 45 to 35, out of 200 traces per window). [TWAIT001, TWAIT002]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports a change in timing as a possibility: in the later window, the elapsed time between the completion of A02 and the completion of A08, and between the completion of A06 and the completion of A08, is consistently longer — roughly doubled for A02→A08 (median about 0.9 h to 1.7 h) and about 2.5× for A06→A08 (median about 0.12 h to 0.23 h). Both intervals end at A08, so the behaviour is consistent with longer intervals into A08 from both of its predecessors. Supporting signs: both time items moved upward in every distribution component, each difference exceeds all but about 1 in 2000 random re-splits of the pooled data, and the time family produced 2 qualifying items where roughly 0.012 would be expected if nothing had changed, while the control-flow family produced 0 items against about 0.29 expected, so the structure around these activities shows no qualifying change. [TWAIT001, TWAIT002]

Limitations: the two items share A08 and likely reflect one underlying difference rather than two independent confirmations; TWAIT measures elapsed time between consecutive completion events, so the evidence does not show where within the interval the extra time arises. A competing explanation that cannot be ruled out is that the additional elapsed time comes from a delay anywhere between the predecessor's completion and A08's completion (including any unobserved intervening behaviour) rather than being tied to A08 itself; the modest drop in observed pairs (40→33, 45→35) is within what finite samples can produce, as no control-flow item qualified. [TWAIT001, TWAIT002]

Screening: 84 units tested, 0.3 items expected without change. By family:
- control_flow: 59 units tested, 0 items, 0.29 expected
- time: 25 units tested, 2 items, 0.012 expected

So the time family has 2 items when 0.012 would be expected by chance. That's many times larger than the expectation (2 vs 0.012 is ~167x). The control flow family has 0 items when 0.29 expected — consistent with no change.

The instruction says: "A count many times larger cannot be explained by chance as a whole, even when all items describe one underlying difference; do not merge items for this comparison." So 2 items vs 0.012 expected is many times larger — this passes the screening comparison. So we don't automatically go to "Insufficient evidence" — we judge by directness, consistency, and ability to rule out competing explanations.

The evidence:
- TWAIT001: T_WAIT between A02 and A08 (elapsed time between consecutive completion events). Before: 40 observations, mean 0.87 hours, median 0.88. After: 33 observations, mean 1.68 hours, median 1.70. So the elapsed time roughly doubled, from about 0.87 to 1.68 hours, an increase of about 0.81 hours. Empirical strength 0.9995 — very unusual for random splits. Support: 40 before, 33 after — moderate counts.
- TWAIT002: T_WAIT between A06 and A08. Before: 45 observations, mean 0.13 hours, median 0.12. After: 35 observations, mean 0.33 hours, median 0.23. Increase of about 0.20 hours. Empirical strength 0.9995. Support: 45 before, 35 after.

Both items involve A08 as the successor. Both show increased elapsed times into A08. Counts decreased slightly (40→33, 45→35), which could be sampling variation.

So the hypothesis: a change in timing — the elapsed time between completion of A02 and A08, and between A06 and A08, increased in the later window. Both transitions converge on A08, suggesting the delay before A08 (or the intervals leading into A08) lengthened. TWAIT is elapsed time between consecutive completion events — not pure waiting/service time. A consistent change in these times is a hypothesis in its own right (a change in timing); it does not need a structural counterpart.
